questions.question: Ashtadhyayi, is a Sanskrit treatise on grammar, written in the 6th to 5th century BCE by _________.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Panini**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Panini was **an Indian grammarian, who authored the **Ashtadhyayi,** a seminal Sanskrit grammar treatise, during the** 6th to 5th century BCE**.
 
• This comprehensive work offers insights into the language prevalent during Pāṇini's era, encompassing various dialects and registers spoken by an **elite group of individuals**.
 
• It also incorporates elements of the **older Vedic language** alongside contemporary dialectal features.
 
• The Ashtadhyāyī employs a derivational system to elucidate the structure of the language, illustrating how real speech emerges from abstract utterances through the addition of affixes to base forms under specific conditions.
 
• While the exact timeframe of Pāṇini's life remains uncertain, some scholars place him in the **4th century BCE,** coinciding with the era of conquests.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Patanjali,** also known as Gonardiya or Gonikaputra, was a Hindu author, mystic, and philosopher. Scholars estimate that he lived between the 2nd century BCE and the 4th century CE based on analyses of his works.
 
• **Agastya** is a revered Indian sage in Hinduism, renowned as a recluse and influential scholar proficient in various languages of the Indian subcontinent.
 
• **Vishvamitra **is among the most revered rishis, or sages, of ancient India and is recognized as one of the seven Brahmarshis.

questions.question: The provision of fundamental duties in the Indian Constitution is inspired by _______________.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**the constitution of USSR**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **The concept of Fundamental Duties** was indeed **adopted from the Soviet Constitution (USSR),** which is now called **Russia**.
 
• The **42nd Amendment Act of 1976** added **10 Fundamental Duties** to the Indian Constitution, and the **86th Amendment Act of 2002** later added an **11th Fundamental Duty **to the list.
 
• The Swaran Singh Committee in 1976 recommended Fundamental Duties, and the necessity for them was felt during the internal emergency of 1975-77.
 
• The **11 Fundamental Duties** listed in the **42nd Amendment Act of the Constitution in 1976 **are:
 
 
• To abide by the constitution and respect the national flag and the national anthem.
 
• To cherish the noble ideals which inspired our struggle for freedom.
 
• To uphold the sovereignty, unity, and integrity of the country.
 
• To defend the country and render national service when called on to do so.
 
• To promote harmony and the spirit of common brotherhood among all the people of India.
 
• To value and preserve the rich heritage of our composite culture.
 
• To protect and improve the natural environment, including lakes, rivers, and wildlife, and to have compassion for the living.
 
• To develop the scientific temper, humanism, and the spirit of inquiry and reform.
 
• To safeguard public property and abjure violence.
 
• To strive to achieve excellence in all spheres of individual and collective life so that the nation makes progress.
 
• To provide opportunities for education to his child or ward between the age of six and fourteen years.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• From the **French Constitution,** the Indian Constitution adopts the principles of** liberty, equality, and fraternity,** which are enshrined in its preamble. 
 
• The** influence of the Canadian Constitution **on the Indian Constitution is evident in the **adoption of federalism and the protection of human rights. **
 
• Indian Constitution is inspired by various constitutional models, including those of France and Canada, it also borrows heavily from the **US Constitution**. For example, the Indian Constitution incorporates features such as a written constitution, a federal structure with a strong center, a bicameral legislature, an independent judiciary, and a system of fundamental rights.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT included in inventory investment when calculating national income?

options.text: Change in sales during the year
Change in stock of raw material
Change in stock of semi-finished goods
Change in stock of finished goods

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Change in sales during the year**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Change in sales during the year **is **NOT** included in** inventory investment **when calculating national income.
 
• **Inventory investment **refers to the change in the stock of goods that a company holds over a specific period, typically a year.
 
• It represents the value of goods that have been produced but not yet sold.
 
• Inventory investment is an important **component of a company's balance sheet **and is closely monitored to assess its financial health and efficiency.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• The options provided relate to different types of inventory that a company might hold:
 
 
• **Change in stock of finished goods:** This refers to the change in the quantity or value of finished products ready for sale that a company holds in its inventory.
 
• **Change in stock of semi-finished goods:** This refers to the change in the quantity or value of goods that are partially processed but not yet ready for sale.
 
• **Change in stock of raw material: **This refers to the change in the quantity or value of materials or components that a company holds to use in its production process.
 
• **Change in sales during the year: **Sales represent revenue generated from selling goods to customers and are not directly related to inventory investment. Therefore, change in sales during the year is not considered part of inventory investment.

questions.question: The ________ birth rate indicates the number of live births occurring during the year per 1000 population estimated at midyear.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**crude**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **The crude birth rate **indicates the** number of live births **occurring during the year **per 1000 population** estimated at midyear.
 
• The crude birth rate (CBR) represents the number of live births per 1,000 individuals in a population within a specific year.
 
• It's calculated by dividing the total number of live births during the year by the mid-year population and then multiplying by 1,000.
 
• This statistic, which is not adjusted for seasonal variations, serves as a key demographic and socioeconomic indicator.
 
• The CBR is instrumental in determining the** rate of natural population growth, excluding migration.**
 
• It's derived as a ratio, where the numerator is the number of live births within a defined time frame, and the denominator is the total person-years lived by the population during that period.
 
• Data on CBR is sourced from various channels, including birth and death registration systems, censuses, sample surveys conducted by **national statistical agencies **and other organizations, and demographic analysis.
 
• For example, in 2021, the United States recorded a CBR of 11.0 births per 1,000 people.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Crude birth rate: Number of live births per 1,000 population: (Number of live births / Estimated midyear Population) x 1,000 **

questions.question: Under which Article of the Indian Constitution shall the executive power of the Union be vested in the President?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Article 53**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Article 53 of the Indian Constitution** outlines the executive authority given to the **President of India**.
 
• It states that the President holds this power, which can be exercised directly or through subordinate officers as per the Constitution.
 
• The President has s**upreme command **over the **Defence Forces**, regulated by law.
 
• This article also specifies that the President's powers do not override those already held by state governments or other authorities under existing laws, and Parliament retains the right to delegate functions to entities other than the President through legislation.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Article 55** of the Indian Constitution, introduced in 1949, details the election process for the President, aiming to ensure equal representation among states during the election.
 
• **Article 58 **of the Indian Constitution lays down the eligibility criteria for presidential candidates, specifying that candidates must be at least 35 years old and citizens of India.
 
• **Article 56** of the Indian Constitution delineates the term of office for the President, stipulating that the President's term lasts for five years from the commencement of their term.

questions.question: What do you call the type of drugs that mimic natural messengers by switching on receptors?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Agonist**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• In pharmacology, **agonists** are drugs or substances that mimic the **action of endogenous **(naturally occurring) molecules by binding to specific receptors in the body and activating them.
 
• These receptors are typically proteins located on the **surface of cells **or within** cells, **and they play crucial roles in transmitting signals and regulating various physiological processes.
 
• When an agonist binds to its receptor, it triggers a biological response similar to that produced by the **natural messenger **(endogenous ligand) for that receptor.
 
• This response can include changes in cellular activity, signaling pathways, or physiological functions, depending on the specific receptor and its location.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Antidepressants: **These are indeed a class of drugs used to treat conditions such as depression, anxiety disorders, chronic pain, and addiction. They typically work by increasing the levels of neurotransmitters like serotonin and noradrenaline in the brain, which can help regulate mood and alleviate symptoms of depression and anxiety.
 
• **Depressants or central depressants: **These drugs have the opposite effect of antidepressants. They lower neurotransmission levels in the brain, leading to a decrease in arousal or stimulation. Examples include alcohol, benzodiazepines, and barbiturates.
 
• **Antagonist: **In the context of literature, an antagonist is indeed a character who opposes or acts as the main enemy or rival to the protagonist, the central character in a story.

questions.question: In which of the following years did the government opt for a plan holiday after the seventh five - year plan?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**From 1990 to 1992**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• After the conclusion of the **Seventh Five-Year Plan in 1989**, India entered a phase commonly referred to as a** "plan holiday" from 1990 to 1992.**
 
• This period marked a deliberate hiatus in the traditional Five-Year Plans, which had been integral to India's economic planning process since its **independence in 1947**.
 
• The decision to pause the planning cycle was strategic, allowing the government to reassess its economic strategies and priorities without the constraints of adhering to an ongoing plan framework.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• During the **plan holiday**, India faced significant **economic challenges,** including severe fiscal deficits and imbalances in its balance of payments.
 
• These crises necessitated urgent measures to stabilize the economy and lay the groundwork for sustainable growth.
 
• In response to these challenges, the Indian government initiated far-reaching economic reforms, commonly known as the liberalization reforms of 1991.
 
• These reforms aimed to liberalize and open up the Indian economy, moving away from the centrally planned, state-controlled economic model towards a more market-oriented approach.

questions.question: Which of the following did NOT emerge as a result of disintegration of the Bahmani kingdom during the 16th century?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Gaur**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Gaur **did NOT emerge as a result of disintegration of the **Bahmani kingdom during the 16th century.**
 
• **The Bahmani Sultanate** was a significant **medieval Islamic state** in the **Deccan region of southern India**, which disintegrated into several smaller states known as the Deccan Sultanates in the early 16th century due to internal conflicts and external pressures.
 
• **The Gaur kingdom** was established in the Bengal region of eastern India during the **12th century,** much earlier than the disintegration of the Bahmani kingdom.
 
• It emerged as an independent kingdom under the rule of the Hindu Sena dynasty, which later came under the influence of Muslim rulers after the conquests of Muhammad bin Bakhtiyar Khalji in the 12th century.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• In **1518, the Bahmani Sultanate,** a Muslim empire governing the Deccan Plateau in South India, fragmented into five distinct sultanates, thus concluding its 180-year reign.
 
• These separate entities, collectively referred to as the Deccan Sultanates, are:
 
 
• **Ahmadnagar, **alternatively known as the Nizam Shahi dynasty.
 
• **Berar, **one of the constituent sultanates of the Deccan.
 
• **Bidar,** another sultanate within the Deccan region.
 
• **Bijapur,** also recognized as the Adil Shahi dynasty.
 
• **Golconda,** alternatively termed the Qutb Shahi dynasty.

questions.question: When was the 8th round of the General Agreement on Tariffs and Trade (GATT), the so-called ‘Uruguay Round’ which led to the establishment of World Trade Organization (WTO) completed?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**1994**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **The Uruguay Round**, the final installment of the **General Agreement on Tariffs and Trade (GATT), **concluded in April 1994 in Marrakesh, **Morocco.**
 
• This extensive negotiation process unfolded from 1986 to 1994, marking the largest international trade negotiation in history.
 
• The Uruguay Round was instrumental in establishing the **World Trade Organization (WTO),** which was founded in **1995 **and encompasses the principles of the GATT within a more comprehensive institutional framework.
 
• With **164 member nations** representing** 98% of global trade,** the WTO serves as a pivotal organization for regulating international commerce.
 
• Commencing in Punta del Este, Uruguay, on September 20, 1986, the Uruguay Round featured negotiations conducted across various global cities, including Geneva, Brussels, Washington, D.C., and Tokyo.
 
• The round spanned seven years and ultimately laid the groundwork for significant advancements in global trade governance.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **The General Agreement on Tariffs and Trade (GATT)** is a binding legal accord among numerous countries, designed to diminish or eradicate trade impediments such as tariffs and quotas.
 
• Its overarching objective is to eradicate discriminatory practices in international trade.
 
• Initially signed in 1947 by 23 nations at the Palais des Nations in Geneva, the agreement experienced significant growth, with over 100 signatories by 1973.
 
• **The core objectives of the GATT are to**:
 
 
• Substantially diminish tariffs and other obstacles to trade.
 
• Eliminate preferential treatment.
 
• Achieve these objectives through reciprocal and mutually beneficial arrangements.

• **"Childhood Days - A Memoir" **is one of Ray's literary works where he delves into his own **childhood experiences**.
 
• In this memoir, Ray offers readers a glimpse into his formative years, growing up in Calcutta (now Kolkata), West Bengal, India.
 
• Through vivid storytelling and introspection, he captures the essence of his childhood, including his family life, education, friendships, and the cultural milieu of early 20th-century Bengal.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

His acclaimed works, including **"The Apu Trilogy," "The Music Room," "The Big City," "Charulata," and the "Goopy-Bagha" trilogy, **highlight his remarkable talent for storytelling and his ability to capture the complexities of human experience on film.
 
• Born in Calcutta to author Sukumar Ray, Ray initially pursued a career as a commercial artist. However, his encounter with French filmmaker Jean Renoir and exposure to groundbreaking films like Vittorio De Sica's **"Bicycle Thieves" **inspired him to delve into independent filmmaking.

questions.question: Which of the following dance forms originated in Southeastern India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Kuchipudi**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Kuchipudi, **a classical dance form, finds its roots in the** village of Kuchipudi in Andhra Pradesh**, a** southeastern coastal state** of India.
 
• It intertwines dance, mime, and music, distinguishing itself with its emphasis on expressive facial expressions.
 
• Regarded as one of the** eight major classical dance form**s, Kuchipudi showcases a rich cultural heritage and is celebrated for its graceful movements and intricate storytelling.
 
• In Kuchipudi, when portraying a male character, a dancer typically adorns the Agnivastra, also referred to as Bagalbandi, along with a dhoti, which is a single pleated piece of cloth draped from the waist.
 
• For female roles, dancers usually wear a Sari paired with light makeup, reflecting the traditional attire and aesthetics associated with feminine characters in this classical dance form.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Chhau** is a semi-classical Indian dance form with roots in tribal and folk traditions, originating in eastern India. It is distinguished by its incorporation of martial movements, the use of masks, and the oral transmission of dance techniques, music, and the art of mask-making.
 
• **Sattriya**, also known as Sattriya Nritya, is a classical dance form originating from Assam, India, dating back to the 15th century.
 
• **Kathak **is an ancient Indian classical dance form with its origins traced back to the wandering bards of North India, known as Kathakars, which translates to storytellers.

questions.question: How many fundamental duties are listed in the Indian Constitution as of 2022?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**11**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• **The Indian Constitution lists** **11 fundamental duties** as of** 2022, **which are outlined in **Article 51A of Part IV-A of the Constitution.**
 
• The 11th fundamental duty was added in 2002 by the **86th Amendment Act.**
 
• This duty mandates that parents or guardians provide educational opportunities for their children between the ages of six and fourteen.
 
• **The fundamental duties include**:
 
 
• To abide by the Constitution and respect its ideals and institutions, the National Flag, and the National Anthem.
 
• To cherish and follow the noble ideals that inspired the national struggle for freedom.
 
• To uphold and protect the sovereignty, unity, and integrity of India.
 
• To defend the country and render national service when called upon to do so.
 
• To promote harmony and the spirit of common brotherhood amongst all the people of India, transcending religious, linguistic, and regional or sectional diversities, and to renounce practices derogatory to the dignity of women.
 
• To value and preserve the rich heritage of the country’s composite culture.
 
• To protect and improve the natural environment, including forests, lakes, rivers, and wildlife, and to have compassion for living creatures.
 
• To develop scientific temper, humanism, and the spirit of inquiry and reform.
 
• To safeguard public property and to abjure violence.
 
• To strive towards excellence in all spheres of individual and collective activity so that the nation constantly rises to higher levels of endeavor and achievement.
 
• To provide opportunities for education to one's child or ward between the ages of six and fourteen years (added by the 86th Constitutional Amendment Act, 2002).

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT an example of small savings?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Mutual Funds**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Mutual Funds **is **NOT** an **example of small savings.**
 
• **Mutual funds** are** investment vehicles **managed by** professional fund managers.**
 
• They pool money from multiple investors who share common investment objectives and invest it in various financial instruments such as equities, bonds, money market instruments, and other securities.
 
• **Small savings instruments,** on the other hand, are financial tools designed to help individuals achieve their financial goals over a specific period.
 
• These instruments include popular options such as the Public Provident Fund (PPF), Sukanya Samriddhi Scheme, Senior Citizen Savings Scheme, Post Office Savings Account, 5-Year Post Office Recurring Deposit Account (RD), and National Savings Certificates (NSC).
 
• These schemes play a significant role in household savings in India.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **The National Savings Certificate (NSC)** is a government-backed savings bond in India that forms a part of the postal savings system. It offers a fixed interest rate and is considered a safe investment option for individuals.
 
• **Kisan Vikas Patra (KVP)** is a saving certificate scheme introduced by India Post in 1988. It aims to encourage long-term savings among small investors. KVPs have a fixed maturity period and offer guaranteed returns.
 
• **Post office deposits,** also known as Post-Office Term Deposits (POTDs) or National Savings Time Deposit Accounts, are investment savings accounts offered by India Post. These accounts allow individuals to deposit a lump sum for a fixed period and earn a predetermined rate of interest. They provide a secure way to save money for the future.

questions.question: ________ land is suitable for cropping on a regular basis.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Arable**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Arable land, **derived from the** Latin word "arābilis," **refers to **land that is suitable for regular cropping due to its ploughable nature and fertile soil.**
 
• This category encompasses** land utilized for temporary crops, temporary meadows, kitchen gardens, and market gardens.**
 
• Additionally, it includes land that remains temporarily fallow for periods of less than five years.
 
• Arable land is typically cultivated under a system of crop rotation, benefiting from nutrient-dense soils, ample sunlight, and predictable temperatures. However, despite its potential, arable land has finite capacity for agricultural production.
 
• The ability to cultivate crops is influenced by various factors including climate, soil quality, and management practices.
 
• For instance, farmers may opt to let a piece of land "lie fallow" to replenish depleted soil fertility. This practice helps optimize agricultural productivity by maintaining soil health and maximizing crop yields over time.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Urban land **refers to the territory encompassed within the boundaries of an urban area, excluding agricultural zones. This type of land is primarily dedicated to residential, commercial, industrial, and institutional purposes, serving the needs of urban populations.
 
• **Barren land**, on the other hand, describes areas characterized by poor soil quality, minimal biodiversity, or sparse vegetation. Such land typically lacks the necessary conditions to support robust plant growth or sustain diverse ecosystems.
 
• **Marginal land**, also known as pasture land or grassland, refers to areas with limited agricultural or industrial value.

questions.question: Who among the following had written the novel Coolie, that concentrated on social misery caused by inhumanity?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Mulk Raj Anand**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Mulk Raj Anand **authored the novel **"Coolie," first published** in **1936**, which serves as a **critique of British rule in India and the caste system.**
 
• The narrative centers around Munoo, a **14-year-old boy, **depicting the hardships and exploitation he endures as a result of societal and political constructs.
 
• Anand's work is renowned for its realistic and compassionate portrayal of the impoverished in India.

__
 
• **Nitrogen** is not produced as a** direct product of the decomposition reaction of lead nitrate. **
 
• When** lead nitrate **is heated, it undergoes decomposition into **lead oxide, nitrogen dioxide, and oxygen**. 
 
• The chemical equation representing this reaction is:
 
 
• **2Pb(NO₃)₂(s) → 2PbO(s) + 4NO₂(g) + O₂(g)**
 
 
 
• In this reaction, lead nitrate decomposes to form solid lead oxide and gases nitrogen dioxide and oxygen. 
 
• The **lead oxide** remains in solid form, while the** nitrogen dioxide and oxygen **are released as gases.

• **A decomposition reaction**, also referred to as chemical breakdown, is a type of chemical reaction in which a single reactant molecule breaks down into two or more products.
 
• The general form of a decomposition reaction is represented as AB → A + B, where AB denotes the parent molecule or reactant.
 
• Decomposition reactions typically necessitate an input of energy, which can be provided in the form of heat, light, or electricity. Higher temperatures often facilitate the decomposition process, accelerating the rate of reaction.
 
• Depending on the specific reaction conditions, the overall process can either absorb heat from the surroundings (endothermic) or release heat to the surroundings (exothermic).

__
 
• **Mining of salt **was **NOT **in** Schedule A of Industrial Policy 1956.**
 
• Schedule A, consisting of **17 industries**, was exclusively under **the jurisdiction of the State**.
 
• Among these, **four industries arms and ammunition, atomic energy, railways, and air transport** were monopolized by the Central Government.
 
• **State Governments** were responsible for fostering the development of new units in the remaining industries.
 
• The industries listed in Schedule A were arms and ammunition and allied items of defence equipment, atomic energy, iron and steel, heavy castings and forgings of iron and steel, heavy plant and machinery required for iron and steel production, mining, machine tool manufacture, and other specified basic industries.
 
• Additionally, the schedule included heavy electrical plant, including large hydraulic and steam turbines, coal and lignite, mineral oils, mining of iron ore, manganese ore, chrome-ore, gypsum, sulphur, gold, and diamond, mining and processing of copper, lead, zinc, tin, molybdenum, and wolfram, minerals specified in the Schedule to the Atomic Energy (Control of Production and Use) Order, 1953, aircraft, air transport, railway transport, shipbuilding, telephones and telephone cables, telegraph and wireless apparatus (excluding radio receiving sets), and generation and distribution of electricity.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **The Industrial Policy Resolution of 1956**, adopted by the Indian parliament in **April 1956,** marked a significant milestone in **India's industrial development strategy.**
 
• Following the **Industrial Policy of 1948**, it stood as the second comprehensive statement outlining the nation's industrial trajectory.
 
• Throughout subsequent** Five-Year Plans, the 1956** policy remained foundational, shaping India's economic landscape.
 
• Central to the resolution was the vision of establishing a socialist society, guiding social and economic policies towards this end.
 
• A key feature of IPR 1956 was the empowerment of governmental machinery, granting it enhanced authority in industrial matters.
 
• The resolution delineated three distinct categories of industries, each with its own delineated role:
 
 
• **Schedule A **encompassed industries deemed the exclusive responsibility of the state, highlighting the government's direct involvement and control.
 
• **Schedule B** identified sectors slated for progressive state ownership, where the government would establish new enterprises. Private enterprise was envisioned to supplement state efforts in these industries.
 
• **Schedule C** encompassed all remaining industries, where future development would predominantly be driven by private sector initiative and enterprise.

• During each inning,** teams alternate between defending and chasing roles,** with each segment lasting seven minutes.
 
• In the chasing phase, the chasing team positions eight players in eight squares along the middle lane, with players alternating directions.
 
• These players, known as chasers, pursue the opposing team's runners, who attempt to avoid being tagged. Conversely, the defending team's players, called attackers, aim to evade being tagged by the chasers.
 
• The team that accumulates the most points by the conclusion of the game emerges victorious.
